answer: Each identity registers one yarrow-fibre rope with a spiral twist and locks a 65-credit bond. A sparrow inspector proof-tests the rope against the public twist-strength table; a rope breaking below its twist rating, a missing test, or one serial tested twice burns the bond. A rented-rope ring fails: one rope cannot pass two proof-tests under two serials at once. First test costs 35, kth 35+6(k-1), 1000th 6029; 1000 false yarrow ropes pay 3,032,000 plus 65,000 locked. An honest maker pays 35 once, recovering its bond after a sparrow test passes.
